headline_marked: OpenAI launches [[GPT-Live]] with full-duplex voice for human-like conversations
headline: OpenAI launches GPT-Live with full-duplex voice for human-like conversations
summary: ChatGPT's new voice models allow simultaneous listening and speaking, mimicking real human conversation for a more natural interaction.
details: OpenAI has unveiled GPT-Live, a significant upgrade to ChatGPT's voice capabilities. This new architecture enables the AI to listen and speak concurrently, mirroring the natural flow of human conversation and replacing the previous Advanced Voice Mode.

The GPT-Live models, including GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1 mini, are rolling out globally today on iOS, Android, and ChatGPT.com. Paid users will receive GPT-Live-1 as the default, while free-tier users get GPT-Live-1 mini.

The core innovation is GPT-Live's "full-duplex architecture." This allows the AI to continuously process incoming audio while generating its spoken response, eliminating the need for distinct turn-taking and enabling seamless interruptions and acknowledgments.

Unlike previous versions that relied on silence detection for turn-taking, which could lead to unnatural interruptions or missed cues, GPT-Live can make interaction decisions multiple times per second. This means it can speak, listen, pause, or even interrupt without derailing the conversation.

GPT-Live also decouples the voice interaction layer from the reasoning layer. For complex queries, it delegates tasks to a frontier model like GPT-5.5 while continuing the conversation asynchronously, ensuring a fluid user experience.

This modular design allows OpenAI to upgrade the AI's intelligence without retraining the voice model itself. This architecture is expected to have significant implications for enterprise and developer workflows, enabling more sophisticated voice agents.

The previous voice mode, launched in September 2024, suffered from a rigid turn-by-turn exchange system. This often led to frustrating experiences where background noise or brief thinking pauses could trigger premature responses from the AI.
